body:
> **Narrowed 2026-10-17 (backlog sweep).**
>
> **Resolved so far:** PR #1029 (`fix/labels-prices-contract`, `a141803a7`).
> - Proposed fix 1: the `units=` docstring now says `food_acquired.Price` is whatever the country's source recorded and that `'unitprice'`/`'unitvalue'` (and `'kgprice'`/`'kgvalue'`) are not guaranteed independent.
> - Proposed fix 2, Uganda: the per-wave raw and served agreement table is in `Uganda/_/CONTENTS.org` (served purchased 94.38-99.94 %, produced 95.25-99.99 %), plus a newly recorded idiosyncrasy: from 2018-19 the purchased `market` price is the library's row median of the three per-leg prices `CEB14a/b/c` (`uganda.py:389-390`), including the own-production leg.
>
> **Remaining (this issue):**
> - (b) Record `Price` provenance in `CONTENTS.org` for the other four `Price`-bearing countries -- elicited, back-calculated by the statistics office, or built by the library. Same-day agreement shares: Panama 100%, GhanaLSS 100% (produced rows only; probably the registered `8h-farmgate` derivation, unconfirmed), Guatemala 97.7%, Serbia 88.5%.
> - (c) Explain Uganda's ~5% raw disagreement in 2009-10 (5.62%) and 2011-12 (5.21%); it is in the raw files and is not the home/away fold.
> - (a) **DECISION:** the optional read-time diagnostic (warn once when `unitprice` and `unitvalue` agree on >90% of a country's rows) -- build it or drop it.

<details><summary>Original issue text</summary>

## The defect

`food_prices(units='unitprice')` is documented as serving the price the survey
recorded. `lsms_library/transformations.py:1368-1372`:

> ``'unitprice'``: reported ``Price`` (currency / native u).
> NaN where **the survey did not record a unit price**.  This mode reflects the
> canonical ``food_acquired.Price`` column — **market price** for ``s='purchased'``,
> **farmgate** for ``s='produced'``, imputed for ``s='inkind'``.

For Uganda that is not what the column holds. UBOS's "Market Price" columns are
**back-calculated `Expenditure / Quantity`**, not independently elicited prices,
so `units='unitprice'` and `units='unitvalue'` return the same number on 94.4-99.9%
of rows -- and a user who reads the docstring will treat them as two independent
sources and get a spurious agreement.

(Note on wording: `slurm_logs/price_sources/Uganda/REPORT.org` D5 paraphrases the
docstring as documenting `unitprice` as *"the survey's own price question"*. The
literal text is quoted above; the paraphrase is fair but is not a verbatim quote,
so the exact string is given here instead.)

## Instances

| country | wave(s) | table | count | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Uganda | all eight | `food_acquired.Price` / `food_prices(units='unitprice')` | share of purchased rows whose reported "Market Price" differs from `Expenditure/Quantity` by more than 1e-6, by wave: **1.72 / 5.62 / 1.09 / 5.21 / 1.51 / 0.06 / 0.08 / 0.09 %** (2005-06 … 2019-20), n = 24,697–35,982 per wave. Median log ratio **0.0** in every wave; pooled median gap 0.000, IQR 0.000, over 4,686 cells | `slurm_logs/price_sources/Uganda/REPORT.org` §2. **Re-verified on the raw `.dta` before the library touches anything**: `h15bq12` against `(h15bq5+h15bq7)/(h15bq4+h15bq6)` gives 1.72% / 5.21% / 1.51% differing in 2005-06 / 2011-12 / 2013-14, and the same holds for the farmgate pair (`Value_own/Qty_own`: 1.36% / 4.75% / 1.01%). The residual few percent is **not** the home/away purchase-leg fold -- among differing rows, only 0.8% / 0.4% / 0.2% have both legs populated |

## Why it matters

This is a documentation defect with a measurable analytic consequence. The whole
point of separating `unitprice` from `unitvalue` is that one is elicited and the
other is derived, so an analyst can check them against each other. For Uganda they
are the same quantity wearing two names: any comparison of the two "sources" for
Uganda returns a median log gap of exactly 0.000 and looks like a triumphant
validation, when it is an identity. The price comparison had to **drop source 2 for
Uganda entirely** on the strength of the raw-file check above.

The docstring is not wrong in general -- for countries that do elicit a price it
describes the column correctly. It is wrong in that it offers no way to tell which
kind of country you are holding, and it currently reads as a guarantee.

## Proposed fix

A docs change in library code, plus optionally one cheap diagnostic:

1. Amend the `units=` docstring in `transformations.py` to say that
   `food_acquired.Price` is **whatever the country's source recorded**, which in
   some countries (Uganda measured; check the other `Price`-bearing countries) is
   the statistical office's own `Expenditure / Quantity` rather than an elicited
   price -- so `'unitprice'` and `'unitvalue'` are not guaranteed independent.
2. Record the distinction per country where it is known, next to the `Price`
   column's provenance in `CONTENTS.org`. Uganda's is documented in
   `slurm_logs/price_sources/Uganda/REPORT.org` §2.
3. Optionally, a one-line diagnostic: if `unitprice` and `unitvalue` agree on
   >90% of a country's rows, the column is derived, and saying so once at read
   time would save every future user this measurement.

Related: #828 (`units='unitprice'` returns an empty frame **silently** where a
country has no `Price` at all -- 6 countries). That issue is the "no price" case;
this one is the "a price that is not a price" case.

Surfaced by the five-source price comparison, 2026-09-08; per-country evidence in `slurm_logs/price_sources/Uganda/REPORT.org`; pattern `P05-price-absent` in `slurm_logs/price_sources/DATA_PROBLEMS.csv`.

</details>
title: Price provenance: is Price elicited or derived for Panama/GhanaLSS/Guatemala/Serbia; explain Uganda's ~5% gap; decide on a read-time diagnostic
